{{Recipe}}

'''Native jollof rice''' is a popular rice dish common among every tribe in Nigeria. It is similar to regular jollof rice, but the native version uses palm oil and other traditional Nigerian ingredients.

==Ingredients==
* A few pieces of [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomato]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]]
* A few fresh Scotch bonnet or [[Cookbook:Habanero|habanero]] [[Cookbook:Chiles|peppers]] (ata rodo)
* ½ [[Cookbook:Units of measurement#Nigeria|milk cup]] [[Cookbook:Ground Crayfish|cround crayfish]]
* [[Cookbook:Iru|Fermented locust bean (iru)]]
* [[Cookbook:Palm Oil|Palm oil]]
* Meat [[Cookbook:Stock|stock]] or water
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
* 4 pieces [[Cookbook:Bouillon Cube|bouillon cubes]] (or the equivalent amount of powder)
* 3 milk cups [[Cookbook:Rice|uncooked rice]]
* 2 tins of cooked [[Cookbook:Mackerel|titus fish]] (optional)
* [[Cookbook:Beef|Beef]], [[Cookbook:Turkey|turkey]], and/or [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] meat (optional), [[Cookbook:Boiling|boiled]]
* Sliced [[Cookbook:Scent Leaf|scent leaf]] (optional)

== Special equipment ==
*Medium-size pot with a cover

== Procedure ==
# [[Cookbook:Puréeing|Blend]] the tomatoes, onions, peppers, and crayfish into a smooth paste.
# Pour the paste into a dry pot on the fire. Cook to evaporate the excess liquid.
# When the water has completely evaporated, add the iru and palm oil. Leave to cook for 10 minutes.
# Add meat stock or water, and bring to [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]]. Adjust seasoning with salt and maggi to taste.
# Wash the rice very well with cold water.
# Add the rice to the boiling stock, and stir well. Add more liquid if necessary, and allow to cook until the rice is almost tender.
# When the rice is almost ready, add the cooked fish or meat. Add the scent leaf, if using.
# Serve the jollof rice hot with plantain (dodo).
